questions.q: Which platform component most directly solves Northline's problem of two data scientists independently building incompatible 'customer lifetime value' feature definitions?
options: An on-call rotation
A canary deployment process
A central feature store with a single registered definition per feature, shared across online and offline use
A rollback strategy
questions.explain: A feature store (Chapter 2) is designed exactly to prevent duplicate, conflicting feature definitions by giving each feature one registered, shared definition and owner.

questions.q: What would most directly have reduced the blast radius of the four-hour fraud-model outage caused by a missing feature?
options: A blameless postmortem
A canary deployment with an approval gate, limiting the new version to a small fraction of traffic before full rollout
A stricter password policy
Retraining the model more frequently
questions.explain: Canary deployments (Chapter 5) expose a new version to a small fraction of traffic first, so a problem like a missing feature is caught before it affects 100% of production traffic.

questions.q: Why should Northline's fraud-detection models and its weekly batch pricing model NOT share the same SLO targets?
options: SLOs can only be defined for batch-scored models
They have very different criticality and latency profiles — a real-time fraud decision path needs much tighter targets than a periodic batch job
Pricing models are not allowed to have SLOs
Fraud models never need an SLO because they are the oldest model
questions.explain: SLOs should be scoped per model based on how that model is actually used — a real-time, high-stakes endpoint needs tighter latency and availability targets than an infrequent batch job.

questions.q: In the suggested build sequence for Northline, why is the model registry recommended as the FIRST piece of infrastructure to build?
options: It is the most expensive component and should be budgeted for first
It is relatively cheap to stand up and immediately resolves the most painful unknown — what model version is actually live
It requires the feature store to already exist
Registries are only useful once on-call rotations exist
questions.explain: The registry is comparatively cheap and solves the most acute, immediate pain point: resolving 'what's live' when nobody currently knows.

questions.q: Why is 15 models described as roughly the 'inflection point' for Northline, rather than, say, 2 or 3 models?
options: Because exactly 15 is a hard technical limit in all ML platforms

Because at that scale, the cost of inconsistency across models (duplicate features, unclear versions, ad hoc on-call) multiplies enough that shared infrastructure becomes cheaper than continuing ad hoc
Because 15 is the maximum number of models any feature store can support
Because regulatory requirements only apply above 15 models
questions.explain: The inflection point is about the economics of ad hoc tooling breaking down as more models share no common infrastructure, not an arbitrary numeric limit on any one tool.
